claims.text: The shop is a noodle maker producing wheat noodles in-house, so flour and wheat are pervasive throughout the kitchen; cross-contact would be unavoidable.
Both broths are animal-based (pork/chicken or fish dashi) and prepared in the same small kitchen, so any item would share equipment with meat and fish stocks.

name: ジェラテリア フィオレ (Gelateria Fiore)

claims.text: Ingredients are sourced carefully and named openly (Hokkaido milk, Nara Kotoka strawberries, Wakayama peaches), which can make it easier to ask staff what is in a given flavor.

name: 元喜神 奈良店 (Genkishin Nara)

claims.text: Wheat is central and unavoidable here: house-made wheat ramen/tsukemen noodles, wheat gyoza wrappers, and shared cookware make this unsafe for celiacs.
All broths are chicken-based (tori paitan from chicken bones, whole chicken and Yamato chicken); toppings include char siu, egg and shrimp. No vegan preparation reported.
Set meals here use standard Japanese seasonings (soy sauce, miso); no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
Miso soup and dishes use fish-based dashi typical of Japanese home cooking; the single daily set commonly includes meat or seafood.
Menu includes fried breaded items (tonkatsu) and wheat-based dishes; no separation or gluten-free handling is documented.
Standard Japanese home cooking; assumes ordinary wheat-containing soy sauce and miso. No wheat-free soy sauce documented.
Sets center on fish and meat with fish-dashi miso soup; no vegan preparation documented.
The shariapin sauce is described as a Japanese-style base made with soy sauce and red wine; standard soy sauce contains wheat.
Menu is built around gyoza, noodles (dan dan, stir-fried ramen) and soy/doubanjiang seasonings, so shared wheat surfaces and sauces are inherent; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Dishes use standard Chinese/Japanese soy-based seasonings (gyoza dipping sauces, mapo tofu), which contain wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Even tofu dishes such as mapo tofu are prepared in the Sichuan style with meat, and the kitchen emphasizes pork, chicken and seafood, so vegan separation is not documented.
Plenty of fresh whole fruit, fruit juices and smoothies are on the menu, which gives plant-based and gluten-avoiding visitors some naturally simpler options to ask about.
